answer_text:
A convenient example is

\[
f(x)=x^4-10x^2+1.
\]

We verify that its Galois group over \(\mathbb{Q}\) is the desired Klein four subgroup of \(S_4\).

Let

\[
K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2,\sqrt3).
\]

This is a biquadratic extension, so

\[
[K:\mathbb{Q}]=4,
\]

and \(K/\mathbb{Q}\) is Galois with Galois group generated by the sign changes on \(\sqrt2\) and \(\sqrt3\).

Set

\[
\alpha=\sqrt2+\sqrt3.
\]

Its four conjugates over \(\mathbb{Q}\) are

\[
\sqrt2+\sqrt3,\quad \sqrt2-\sqrt3,\quad -\sqrt2+\sqrt3,\quad -\sqrt2-\sqrt3.
\]

Thus the minimal polynomial of \(\alpha\) is

\[
\prod_{\varepsilon,\delta=\pm 1}(x-\varepsilon\sqrt2-\delta\sqrt3).
\]

Grouping the factors,

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x)
&=\bigl(x^2-(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)^2\bigr)\bigl(x^2-(\sqrt2-\sqrt3)^2\bigr)\\
&=\bigl(x^2-(5+2\sqrt6)\bigr)\bigl(x^2-(5-2\sqrt6)\bigr)\\
&=x^4-10x^2+1.
\end{aligned}
\]

So

\[
f(x)=x^4-10x^2+1.
\]

It is irreducible over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Indeed, if it factored into monic quadratics, we would have

\[
x^4-10x^2+1=(x^2+px+q)(x^2-px+r)
\]

with \(p,q,r\in\mathbb{Q}\). Comparing coefficients gives

\[
p(r-q)=0,\qquad q+r-p^2=-10,\qquad qr=1.
\]

If \(p=0\), then \(q+r=-10\) and \(qr=1\), so \(q,r\) would be roots of \(t^2+10t+1\), whose discriminant is \(96\), not a square in \(\mathbb{Q}\). If \(r=q\), then \(q^2=1\), so \(q=\pm1\), and the equation for \(p^2\) becomes \(p^2=12\) or \(p^2=8\), again impossible over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Hence \(f\) is irreducible.

Therefore its splitting field is exactly \(K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2,\sqrt3)\), since all four roots lie in \(K\), and \(K\) has degree \(4\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\).

Label the roots as

\[
\begin{aligned}
r_1&=\sqrt2+\sqrt3,\\
r_2&=\sqrt2-\sqrt3,\\
r_3&=-\sqrt2+\sqrt3,\\
r_4&=-\sqrt2-\sqrt3.
\end{aligned}
\]

The automorphism sending \(\sqrt3\mapsto -\sqrt3\) and fixing \(\sqrt2\) sends

\[
r_1\leftrightarrow r_2,\qquad r_3\leftrightarrow r_4,
\]

so it corresponds to

\[
(12)(34).
\]

The automorphism sending \(\sqrt2\mapsto -\sqrt2\) and fixing \(\sqrt3\) sends

\[
r_1\leftrightarrow r_3,\qquad r_2\leftrightarrow r_4,
\]

so it corresponds to

\[
(13)(24).
\]

Thus

\[
\operatorname{Gal}(f/\mathbb{Q})
=
\langle (12)(34), (13)(24)\rangle
=
V_4\subset S_4.
\]

Therefore a monic polynomial over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with the required Galois group is

\[
\boxed{x^4-10x^2+1}.
\]
